text:
The pion is at rest, so its total energy is just its rest‑mass energy  

\[
E_{\pi}=m_{\pi}c^{2}=139.6\ \text{MeV}.
\]

In the decay \(\pi^{+}\to\mu^{+}+\nu\) the muon (mass \(m_{\mu}=105.7\) MeV) and the (essentially massless) neutrino have equal and opposite momenta \(p\).

Energy conservation:

\[
E_{\pi}=E_{\mu}+E_{\nu}= \sqrt{p^{2}+m_{\mu}^{2}}+p .
\]

Solve for \(p\):

\[
\sqrt{p^{2}+m_{\mu}^{2}} = 139.6 - p
\]
\[
p^{2}+m_{\mu}^{2}= (139.6-p)^{2}
\]
\[
m_{\mu}^{2}=139.6^{2}-2(139.6)p
\]
\[
p = \frac{139.6^{2}-m_{\mu}^{2}}{2\cdot139.6}.
\]

Numerically,

\[
139.6^{2}=1.9488\times10^{4}\ \text{MeV}^2,\qquad
m_{\mu}^{2}=1.1172\times10^{4}\ \text{MeV}^2,
\]

\[
p = \frac{1.9488\times10^{4}-1.1172\times10^{4}}{279.2}
   \approx 2.98\times10^{1}\ \text{MeV}=29.8\ \text{MeV}.
\]

Thus  

* Neutrino energy (all kinetic) \(K_{\nu}=p\approx 29.8\) MeV.  

* Muon total energy \(E_{\mu}=139.6-p\approx 109.8\) MeV, so its kinetic energy  

\[
K_{\mu}=E_{\mu}-m_{\mu}=109.8-105.7\approx 4.12\ \text{MeV}.
\]

Therefore the kinetic energies are \(K_{\mu}\approx4.12\) MeV and \(K_{\nu}\approx29.8\) MeV.

**Answer: A**.
